attrs.evidence: probe_snapshot_v12_repro.mjs, paired and gating: 2/2 reproduce against frozen v0.11.0 copies — P-6, where four reads of one getter place an entrypoint outside its own hashed closure into the frozen internal catalog; and P-6b, where three reads split a registry's key from its value. 5/5 confined live: the catalog getter is read EXACTLY ONCE and the honest entrypoint is stored, the same attack driven end to end through the authority runs the honest worker and leaves the evil worker's startup marker absent, the AST getter is read EXACTLY ONCE so key and value agree by construction rather than by a downstream check, a Map and a function-carrying entry are both refused before any field is examined, and the six rungs are asserted as a set.
attrs.statement: UNTRUSTED DATA MUST BE SEVERED BEFORE IT IS VALIDATED, NOT VALIDATED BEFORE IT IS SEVERED. Every untrusted structure that becomes authority state is canonicalised into an OWNED SNAPSHOT exactly once; validation, identity computation and storage then operate only on that snapshot. NO UNOWNED MUTABLE OBJECT IS CONSULTED TWICE ACROSS A TRUST DECISION. A getter is read as many times as it is written, and the reads need not agree. v0.11.0's executor catalog read `entrypoint` four times — typeof, isAbsolute, the entrypoint-inside-closure check, and then the frozen internal entry — so a getter answering honestly for the three validating reads and maliciously for the fourth put an entrypoint OUTSIDE its own hashed closure into the immutable catalog, and the un-hashed executable really ran while acceptance reported the honest closure's digest. ProgramRegistry.bind had the same shape with a milder outcome: it hashed the caller's AST and then cloned it, so the registry could be keyed by const(5)'s identity while holding const(999). THE MILDER OUTCOME IS NOT A DEFENCE. bind fails closed only because verify() recomputes the id from what was stored — a SECOND mechanism catching the first is not the first working, and authorize() will issue a request against the broken id in the meantime. This is the sixth rung, and the first that is not an object: @1 the implementation LABEL, @2 the registration NAME, @3 the ACTION beside the artifact evidence, @4 the SEMANTIC ORACLE, @5 the AUTHORITY-BEARING OBJECT, @6 MUTABLE DATA READ TWICE. canonicalBytes has refused a capability since v0.1.0; what was not said is that reading THROUGH it twice reintroduces one — the second read IS the capability. The executor catalog is canonical PLAIN DATA only, and a Map is refused: this is a trust boundary whose thesis is that capabilities are not data, and admitting richer JS object forms at it buys nothing.
